newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday Nov 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday Nov 12.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Political dialogue broke down as the centre-right opposition along with secessionist Northern League party left the Lower House where the 1997 budget is under examination. The Freedom Alliance is fiercely opposed to the special powers asked by the government to dictate policy on key budget areas without having to refer back to parliament (all).

* Some ministers from leftist PDS party reportedly threatened to abandon the government because of hard-left Communist Refoundation party "blackmail" to the ruling coalition. Refoundation proved its power by leaving the Lower House for an hour during the parliamentary debate over the budget, so that there was no quorum (Corriere della Sera).
* The government is going to call a confidence vote in Senate upper house to convert into law a decree on a rescue plan for ailing Banco di Napoli (all).
* The Northern League announced elections for the self-proclaimed "Republic of Padania" (all).

* With a surprising move, Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi announced a merger between state telecoms holding Stet with its telephone operator Telecom Italia, but the privatisation of Stet will not take place before autumn 1997. On the Milan stock exchange, Stet rose 6.29 percent while Telecom Italia lost 7.74 percent (all).

* Ciampi also said that the government expects to sell yellow-pages publisher Seat in early 1997 and motorway company Autostrade by June 1997. Meanwhile state holding company IRI has been instructed to sell off either controlling or minority stakes such as those in navigation group Finmare and in Banca di Roma (all).

* Television and advertising group Mediaset said if it did not have to compete for a possible third licence to become the third mobile telephone operator in Italy, it did not rule out interest in second licence holder Omnitel or telecoms holding Stet (all).
* Shares in information technology group Olivetti rose after the sale of an indirect 5.8 percent stake in mobile phone consortium Omnitel to German company Mannesmann (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
